prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: rear-end collision in League City, Texas. The claimant was a driver and reported neck and back strain. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1436; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Officer narrative: Rear-end collision, League City, Texas. Driver 1 reported stopping in slow traffic when the rear of the vehicle was struck by Driver 2's vehicle. A Passenger was also in Driver 1's vehicle, and my observation at the scene and both drivers' statements confirm Driver 1 was present in the vehicle at the time of impact. Driver 1 is the named insured on the policy for the struck vehicle. Driver 1 complained of neck and back strain at the scene. The force of the impact and the vehicle's rear-end deformation are consistent with the injuries described. Scene photographs show damage that largely matches the reported impact point and direction. No prior damage to the vehicle was known to either party or observed during inspection. No independent witnesses were identified, and the account relies on the drivers' statements and the physical evidence at the scene. Driver 2 acknowledged following too closely. Both drivers were advised of reporting requirements, and the vehicles were moved from the travel lane without further incident.
